blocks.content: A custom network, one you explicitly create with docker network create, behaves like the default bridge but with one major practical upgrade: automatic DNS resolution by container name.
docker network create makes a new, user-defined bridge network, containers can then be attached to it explicitly, either at docker run time or afterward.

blocks.alt: A network you create and name yourself

blocks.content:
docker network create mynet
docker run -d --network mynet --name web myapp

code.content:
docker network create mynet
docker run -d --network mynet --name web myapp

codes.bash:
docker network create mynet
docker run -d --network mynet --name web myapp

blocks.content: 2. Automatic DNS Resolution, the Big Upgrade
blocks.text: 2. Automatic DNS Resolution, the Big Upgrade

blocks.content: This is the single biggest practical reason to prefer a custom network over the default bridge: containers on a user-defined network can reach each other by container name directly, Docker runs an embedded DNS server that resolves those names automatically (covered in full in the DNS Resolution topic later in this module).

blocks.alt: Reach another container just by its name, automatically

blocks.content: Custom networks are also a real isolation boundary, containers on one custom network cannot reach containers on a completely different one by default, letting you group related services (an app and its database) together while keeping them separate from unrelated containers on the same host.

blocks.alt: Related services grouped together, isolated from unrelated ones

blocks.content: 4. A Container Can Join More Than One Network
blocks.text: 4. A Container Can Join More Than One Network

blocks.content: Nothing limits a container to a single network, it can be attached to several at once, useful when one service (an API gateway, for instance) needs to bridge traffic between two otherwise-isolated groups of containers.

blocks.alt: One container, attached to multiple networks at once

blocks.content:
docker network connect anothernet web
# "web" is now reachable on both mynet and anothernet

code.content:
docker network connect anothernet web
# "web" is now reachable on both mynet and anothernet

codes.bash:
docker network connect anothernet web
# "web" is now reachable on both mynet and anothernet

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Custom networks add automatic DNS-by-name resolution the default bridge network does not have, the main reason to prefer them.
They also serve as a real isolation boundary between groups of containers, and a container can be attached to more than one at once.
